name: Anaplastic/Large Cell Medulloblastoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System

criteria.description: Presence of large, pleomorphic tumor cells with prominent nucleoli and high mitotic activity
Positive staining for neuronal markers such as synaptophysin and NeuN
Molecular classification consistent with Group 3 or Group 4 medulloblastoma subtypes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of anaplastic/large cell morphology with supportive immunohistochemical markers
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular subgrouping aids prognosis but is not mandatory for diagnosis

searchTerms: rapid worsening of balance and coordination
fast onset unsteady walking and clumsiness

pathognomonic.symptomName: Signs of increased intracranial pressure (e.g., papilledema)
searchTerms: signs of increased pressure inside the skull
head pain worse after waking up

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting related to intracranial hypertension
searchTerms: nausea caused by increased head pressure

common.symptomName: Gait disturbance due to cerebellar dysfunction
searchTerms: unsteady gait due to brain dysfunction

common.symptomName: Diplopia from cranial nerve VI palsy
searchTerms: double vision from nerve VI palsy
cranial nerve six weakness with double vision
cranial nerve seven palsy causing facial droop

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor
unusual changes in behavior or mood

laboratory: CSF cytology may reveal malignant cells in metastatic cases
Elevated CSF protein in some cases
imaging: MRI showing a heterogeneously enhancing mass in the cerebellar vermis or hemispheres
Evidence of hydrocephalus secondary to tumor obstruction
genetic: Molecular subgrouping consistent with Group 3 or Group 4 medulloblastoma
other: Histopathology demonstrating large anaplastic cells with high mitotic index and apoptotic bodies

distinguishingFeatures: Different molecular subgrouping (often WNT or SHH)
Different tumor location (often fourth ventricle floor)

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure (e.g., severe headache, vomiting, papilledema)
references: Louis DN, Perry A, Reifenberger G, et al. The 2021 WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System: a summary. Neuro Oncol. 2021;23(8):1231-1251.
Taylor MD, Northcott PA, Korshunov A, et al. Molecular subgroups of medulloblastoma: the current consensus. Acta Neuropathol. 2012;123(4):465-472.
